references.text: The same expression "God over the spirit in all flesh" is used by Moses when he asks the Lord to appoint a leader for the congregation.
Moses and Aaron fall on their faces again later in the same chapter when the Lord's wrath threatens to wipe out the congregation.
Abraham argues similarly with God to spare the righteous along with the wicked in Sodom.
David asks God to punish him alone and not the people, a similar intercession to spare the innocent.
The principle of individual responsibility for sin: the one who sins shall die, not others on his account.
God is described as the one who holds the soul of all living things and the spirit of every person in His hand.
The spirit returns to God who gave it – God, the Lord of all spirits.
The Lord is the one who created the spirit and the breath of life – affirming His dominion over all spirit.
God is called "the Father of spirits" whom all must submit to.
